introduction.text: The Settecamini archaeological area is a Roman settlement site located in the Settecamini district of Rome, notable for its remains of early Christian and pagan structures, a Roman road, and an Imperial-era mosaic.

history.description: The earliest building is an early Christian structure inserted into a 1st-century BC pagan temple.
The settlement was abandoned in the 5th century.

design.description: The best-preserved building is the taberna, a rest stop for travellers, featuring an Imperial-era mosaic.
A courtyard with a central well that led to two side entrances.

art.description: An Imperial-era mosaic found in the taberna.
